title: Barcelona 1-1 Arsenal: Graham Hansen salvages point as hosts' perfect start ends
subtitle: Arsenal were forced to survive for large parts of Thursday's clash but escaped with a point from Barcelona in the Women's Champions League.
paragraphs: Barcelona's perfect start to their Women's Champions League campaign ended as Caroline Graham Hansen's second-half goal secured a 1-1 draw with Arsenal.

Pere Romeu's side headed into Thursday's clash at Camp Nou as the only side with a 100% record across the first three games, but they needed to come from behind to avoid defeat here after Frida Maanum's 22nd-minute opener against the run of play.
Although Alessia Russo somehow missed a glorious headed chance early on, Arsenal were up against it for large parts of the opening stages.
Graham Hansen soon tested Misa Rodriguez, who then twice denied Esmee Brugts with a double stop before thwarting Sydney Schertenleib.
But Arsenal made their chance count at the other end when Maanum swept home the opening goal after Caitlin Foord had been denied by Cata Coll from Russo's fizzing delivery.
Schertenleib fired over from range, and Patri Guijarro poked wide in response, before Graham Hansen glanced a header wide with the goal at her mercy.
Graham Hansen made amends for that miss just before the hour when she danced inside and finished expertly into the top-left corner, leaving Misa helpless.
Russo skewed over in response before Misa parried Schertenleib's strike deflected off Leah Williamson as Arsenal held on for a vital point.
Graham Hansen should have left on the winning side.
She set up a remarkable 10 chances for her Barcelona team-mates, seven more than the entire Arsenal team combined, and had six shots of her own (only behind seven from Schertenleib).
Graham Hansen also delivered when it mattered; the Norwegian has now been involved in goals in all four of her Champions League games this season (five goals, two assists).
But her brilliance was not enough for victory, even though Barca accumulated 2.25 expected goals (xG) to Arsenal's 1.21 and had 24 shots to their visitors' seven.
The draw leaves Barcelona as the joint leaders, level on 10 points with Lyon, who currently hold top spot due to their superior goal difference, while Arsenal sit fourth, two points behind.
Renee Slegers may take some positives still, given Arsenal are unbeaten in each of their last seven league phase/group-stage games in the Champions League (W5 D2).

Barcelona's perfect start to their Women's Champions League campaign ended as Caroline Graham Hansen's second-half goal secured a 1-1 draw with Arsenal.

Pere Romeu's side headed into Thursday's clash at Camp Nou as the only side with a 100% record across the first three games, but they needed to come from behind to avoid defeat here after Frida Maanum's 22nd-minute opener against the run of play.

Although Alessia Russo somehow missed a glorious headed chance early on, Arsenal were up against it for large parts of the opening stages.

Graham Hansen soon tested Misa Rodriguez, who then twice denied Esmee Brugts with a double stop before thwarting Sydney Schertenleib.

But Arsenal made their chance count at the other end when Maanum swept home the opening goal after Caitlin Foord had been denied by Cata Coll from Russo's fizzing delivery.

Schertenleib fired over from range, and Patri Guijarro poked wide in response, before Graham Hansen glanced a header wide with the goal at her mercy.

Graham Hansen made amends for that miss just before the hour when she danced inside and finished expertly into the top-left corner, leaving Misa helpless.

Russo skewed over in response before Misa parried Schertenleib's strike deflected off Leah Williamson as Arsenal held on for a vital point.

Hansen's on fire

Graham Hansen should have left on the winning side.

She set up a remarkable 10 chances for her Barcelona team-mates, seven more than the entire Arsenal team combined, and had six shots of her own (only behind seven from Schertenleib).

Graham Hansen also delivered when it mattered; the Norwegian has now been involved in goals in all four of her Champions League games this season (five goals, two assists).

But her brilliance was not enough for victory, even though Barca accumulated 2.25 expected goals (xG) to Arsenal's 1.21 and had 24 shots to their visitors' seven.

The draw leaves Barcelona as the joint leaders, level on 10 points with Lyon, who currently hold top spot due to their superior goal difference, while Arsenal sit fourth, two points behind.

Renee Slegers may take some positives still, given Arsenal are unbeaten in each of their last seven league phase/group-stage games in the Champions League (W5 D2).
